sources.title: Victor Guillemin and Alan Pollack, Differential Topology (Prentice-Hall, 1974; complete 236-page PDF)
sources.locator: Ch. 2 §4, printed pp. 77–84 (PDF pp. 91–98); Ch. 3 §3, printed pp. 107–118 (PDF pp. 121–132).
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 236-page PDF (3,472,576 bytes) and extracted the full text with mutool; the file carries an OCR text layer whose running heads identify the printed page numbers, which run fourteen ahead of the PDF page numbers. Read Ch. 2 §4 in full on printed pp. 77–84 (complementary dimension and finite transverse intersections; definition and homotopy invariance of the mod 2 intersection number I_2; the Corollary extending I_2 to arbitrary maps; the torus and Möbius examples; the Boundary Theorem; mod 2 degree and its first applications; Exercises 1–14) and Ch. 3 §3 in full on printed pp. 107–118 (oriented setting and preimage orientation; the local orientation number and the definition of I(f,Z); the propositions for X=∂W and for homotopy invariance; degree and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; the ordered factor convention I(X,Z) versus I(Z,X); map–map intersection, the diagonal Lemma and I(f,g)=(−1)^{dim Z}I(f×g,Δ); I(f,g)=(−1)^{dimX·dimZ}I(g,f); Euler characteristic as I(Δ,Δ); Exercises 1–18). OCR noise in symbols was resolved against the displayed formulas and Figures 2-12 to 2-17 and 3-7 to 3-11.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §4, pp. 77–78: complementary dimension; X ⋔ Z makes X∩Z a finite zero-dimensional set
contents.support: The finiteness statement is exactly the lemma's first clause; the closedness/compactness bookkeeping is supplied by the library's topology items.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §4, pp. 78–79: definition I_2(f,Z)=#f^{-1}(Z) mod 2 and the Theorem that homotopic transversal maps agree
Ch. 2 §4, p. 79: Corollary extending I_2 to arbitrary maps; submanifold definition I_2(X,Z)=I_2(i,Z)
Ch. 2 §4, p. 79, Figure 2-14: I_2(S^1×{1},{1}×S^1)=1 on the torus
Ch. 2 §4, pp. 79–80, Figure 2-15: the Möbius central curve has I_2(X,X)=1 and obstructs orientability
contents.reason: Self-intersection numbers and their Euler-class interpretation are commissioned for the later intersection-pairings page (DT-12); this pair defines the intersection set but does not mint self-intersection or characteristic-class content.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §4, p. 80: Boundary Theorem — X=∂W and g extends to W imply I_2(g,Z)=0
Ch. 2 §4, pp. 80–81: mod 2 degree deg_2(f)=I_2(f,{y}) and its constancy; homotopy invariance
contents.reason: The mod 2 degree as an invariant and its sphere applications are the commissioned subject of the Hopf degree page (DT-18); this pair only recovers the integral degree sign formula on its B page.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §4, pp. 81–82: one-half Fundamental Theorem of Algebra from deg_2(p/|p|)
contents.reason: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra and the zero-counting applications are owned by the complex-analysis pages of this library; the pair consumes only the intersection-theoretic mechanism, not this application.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §4, Exercise 3, pp. 82–83: I_2(f,g):=I_2(f×g,Δ) and its homotopy invariance
Ch. 2 §4, Exercise 13, p. 84: invariance and the Boundary Theorem fail without closed Z, compact X or compact W
Ch. 2 §4, Exercise 14, p. 84: cobordant submanifolds and deformation (the 'trousers' example)
contents.reason: Cobordism of submanifolds and the bordism relation are the commissioned subject of the smooth-cobordism pair (DT-15); the Boundary Theorem needed here is recorded separately.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3, pp. 107–108: oriented setting, preimage orientation, local orientation number, definition of I(f,Z)
Ch. 3 §3, p. 108: Propositions X=∂W ⇒ I(f,Z)=0 and homotopy invariance; extension to arbitrary maps
Ch. 3 §3, pp. 108–109: degree deg(f)=I(f,{y}), the z↦z^m computation and degree as a reduced-value count
Ch. 3 §3, pp. 110–111: total zero count via the degree of p/|p| and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
contents.reason: The multiplicity count of polynomial zeros and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra belong to complex analysis; they are not prerequisites of any item of this pair and are recorded only as the source's application.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3, p. 112: the order of the two factors and the example I(X,Z)=−I(Z,X) (Figure 3-10)
Ch. 3 §3, pp. 113–114: map–map intersection, local sign, diagonal Lemma, I(f,g)=(−1)^{dim Z}I(f×g,Δ)
Ch. 3 §3, p. 115: I(f,g)=(−1)^{(dim X)(dim Z)}I(g,f) and the submanifold corollary
Ch. 3 §3, p. 115: odd-dimensional self-intersection vanishes; Möbius nonorientability from I_2(X,X)=1
contents.reason: Self-intersection and its orientability consequences are commissioned for the intersection-pairings page; the factor-interchange sign they use is proved here.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3, p. 116: the Euler characteristic χ(Y)=I(Δ,Δ) of the diagonal
contents.reason: The diagonal self-intersection as the Euler characteristic is the opening construction of the intersection-pairings page (DT-12), which owns the identification.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3, Exercises 12 and 15, pp. 117–118: direct order computation; f^{-1}(Z) equals the sum of the local submanifold intersections
Ch. 3 §3, Exercise 16, p. 118: I(Z,Z)=I(Z×Z,Δ) for half-dimensional Z
contents.reason: This is the self-intersection special case of the diagonal identification; it is the technical core of the intersection-pairings page (DT-12).

sources.title: John Milnor, Topology from the Differentiable Viewpoint (Princeton University Press; complete 76-page PDF, including the appendix Classifying 1-manifolds)
sources.locator: §2, printed p. 14; §§4–5, printed pp. 20–31 (PDF pp. 31–42); Appendix 'Classifying 1-manifolds', printed pp. 56–57 (PDF pp. 67–68).
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 76-page PDF (1,654,205 bytes) and extracted the full text with mutool. Read §4 in full on printed pp. 20–25 (smooth homotopy and isotopy; the Homotopy Lemma reducing the count to the boundary of a compact 1-manifold, with Figure 6; the Homogeneity Lemma; the mod 2 degree theorem and examples) and §5 in full on printed pp. 26–31 (orientations of vector spaces and manifolds, the boundary orientation convention and the sign of df_x, Theorem A/B for degree, Lemma 1 with Figure 9 showing the two signs −1 and +1 on each arc of F^{-1}(y), Lemma 2 for homotopy invariance, and the examples including the antipodal map and the vector-field application). Read the Appendix 'Classifying 1-manifolds' in full on printed pp. 56–57 (the classification theorem, arc-length parametrizations, the overlap lemma, and the maximal-extension proof), and the citation of the classification on printed p. 14, Lemma 5.

contents.name: §4, pp. 20–22: smooth homotopy and isotopy; Homotopy Lemma and Figure 6, where F^{-1}(y) is a compact 1-manifold
§4, p. 22: the boundary of the compact 1-manifold F^{-1}(y) has evenly many points
§4, pp. 23–25: the mod 2 degree theorem, its homotopy invariance, and examples (constant maps, identity)
contents.reason: The mod 2 degree and the Hopf-type applications are commissioned for the Hopf degree page (DT-18); the count itself is used here only through the parity lemma.

contents.name: §5, pp. 26–28: orientation of a manifold with boundary; the induced boundary sign of a boundary point
§5, pp. 26–27: definition of deg(f;y)=Σ sign df_x over a regular value
§5, pp. 28–29, Lemma 1 and Figure 9: on each arc of F^{-1}(y) the two boundary signs are −1 and +1, so deg(f;y)=0
§5, p. 29, Lemma 2: the oriented product [0,1]×M gives homotopy invariance of degree
§5, pp.30–31: degree examples z↦z^k and the antipodal map
contents.reason: These concrete sphere/circle degree computations are extra applications. The current regular-value intersection example uses the published degree formula and fully proved local signs, with no antipodal or power-map computation as a prerequisite.

contents.name: §5, pp.30–31: nonvanishing vector fields on spheres
contents.reason: The tangent-field obstruction via antipodal degree belongs to the vector-field/Poincare–Hopf commission; it is not a prerequisite of the current compact transverse intersection trace or its parity/sign counts.

contents.name: §2, p. 14, Lemma 5: 'the only compact 1-manifolds are finite disjoint unions of circles and segments', used to force an even boundary
Appendix, pp. 56–57: classification theorem for connected 1-manifolds via arc-length parametrizations, with the overlap lemma and maximal extension

sources.title: Eleny Ionel, notes by Andrew Lin, Stanford Math 215B Differential Topology, Winter 2023 (complete 63-page lecture notes)
sources.locator: Lectures 14–15, document pp. 43–49 (dated February 23 and February 28, 2023).
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 63-page lecture-note PDF (543,433 bytes) and extracted the full text with mutool. Read Lecture 14 on pp. 43–46 (the Thom class and Euler class interface, the Poincaré-dual interpretation of a submanifold, Theorems 134/138/139 and their collapse-map proof through Poincaré–Lefschetz duality) and Lecture 15 on pp. 46–49 (the cap-product convention, the intersection product in homology defined as the Poincaré dual of the cup product, Theorem 140 [P∩Q]=[P]·[Q] with the orientation TM=T(P∩Q)⊕N_P⊕N_Q, the sign [P]·[Q]=(−1)^m[P×Q]·[Δ_M], shriek maps f_![pt]=[f^{-1}(pt)], and degree as Σ sign). The Euler-class/self-intersection continuation on p. 50 was read for its deferral.

contents.name: Lecture 14, pp. 43–44: Thom class, Euler class and the Poincaré-dual interpretation of a submanifold
contents.reason: Thom and Euler classes as cohomological constructions are owned by the algebraic-topology pages and applied on the intersection-pairings page (DT-12); this pair deliberately mints no characteristic classes.

contents.name: Lecture 14, pp. 44–46: Theorems 138/139 (PD[S] is the Thom class of the normal bundle) with the collapse and Poincaré–Lefschetz proof
contents.reason: The identification of the geometric pairing with the Poincare-dual cup pairing is the central theorem of the intersection-pairings page (DT-12); the present pair only fixes the geometric conventions it will consume.

contents.name: Lecture 15, pp. 46–48: intersection product in homology as the Poincare dual of cup product; Theorem 140 and the orientation TM=T(P∩Q)⊕N_P⊕N_Q
contents.support: This is an independent treatment of the ordered normal decomposition that fixes the local sign convention; the homology-side identification is deferred, the orientation content is absorbed here.

contents.name: Lecture 15, p. 48: complementary pairing P·Q in H_0(M)≅Z and the sign [P]·[Q]=(−1)^m[P×Q]·[Δ_M]
Lecture 15, pp. 49–50: f_![pt]=[f^{-1}(pt)] and Corollary 143, deg f=Σ sign(x) over a generic fibre
Lecture 15, p. 50: self-intersection S·S and Theorem 144, the Euler class as the zero locus of a generic section
contents.reason: Self-intersection and the Euler class of the normal bundle are the commissioned core of the intersection-pairings page (DT-12).

contents.name: §4, Figure 6, pp. 22–23: the two endpoint counts of a compact 1-manifold are congruent modulo 2
contents.support: The figure is the picture of two cancelling intersections: counts 2 and 0 with equal parity, which is exactly the mechanism the counterexample displays.
